title: FARDC Accuses AFC/M23-RDF of Fresh Attacks on Walikale-Masisi Axis, Reports Burned Villages and New Displacement
detail: FARDC's Sokola 1 Grand-Nord and Front Nord operational sector, through spokesman Lieutenant Marc Elongo, said Sunday, Sept 20, 2026 that AFC/M23-RDF forces carried out fresh attacks along the Walikale-Masisi axis, burning villages and destroying agricultural fields. The army said the attacks contradict commitments made under the Doha and Washington peace processes and reported new population displacement toward Walikale, without specifying a casualty count or precise damage assessment. North Kivu's military governor and operations commander, Major-General Somo Kakule Évariste, said FARDC "will continue to defend their positions and protect civilians" and would respond to any attack on its positions or on the civilian population. Neither AFC/M23 nor Rwanda had responded to the accusation as of publication.

media.caption: North Kivu's Walikale-Masisi axis, where FARDC accused AFC/M23-RDF forces of burning villages and destroying crops, Sept 20, 2026

confidenceReason: Sourced solely to a named FARDC sector spokesman and the North Kivu military governor's statement via Reporter.cd (tier 3); no independent verification of the attacks, burned villages or displacement, and AFC/M23/Rwanda have not responded.

title: FARDC Reports Village Recaptures on Minembwe Approach as Operation Sukola 2 Sud Pushes Through Fizi Highlands
detail: FARDC's Operation Sukola 2 Sud, through spokesman Lt. Reagan Mbuyi, said forces advancing on multiple axes toward Minembwe-centre in the South Kivu highlands recaptured strategic villages over the weekend of Sept 19-20, 2026, including Natulonge and Nagushushu in Fizi's Lulenge sector. Government troops pushed along the Mulima-Mukoko, Kimete-Kabanja and Mitamba-Masangu axes and secured the Nyamiringa-Mukoko corridor, with operations aimed at further progress toward Kakenge and opening access to Mulambia. The offensive pits FARDC, Wazalendo and allied forces against the AFC/M23-Twirwaneho coalition that has held the Minembwe highlands cluster since mid-2026. Mbuyi declined to give precise casualty figures, saying only that "necessary measures are being taken to protect civilians."

media.caption: FARDC forces advancing through the South Kivu highlands toward Minembwe, Sept 19-20, 2026

confidenceReason: Sourced solely to Operation Sukola 2 Sud's named spokesman via a single Congolese outlet (CongoQuotidien, tier 3); no independent verification of the village recaptures or corridor control, and neither AFC/M23 nor Twirwaneho has responded to the claim.
